name: Voice surgery (cricothyroid approximation)
lead: Cricothyroid approximation (CTA) is a voice surgery that raises pitch by moving the cricoid and thyroid cartilages closer together, tensioning and lengthening the vocal folds. It has mainly been used for voice feminisation in transgender women.[1][2]

Wikipedia reports that CTA often leaves patients locked into falsetto, that outcomes may decline over time, and that fewer clinicians perform it now than Wendler glottoplasty.[1] A 2017 systematic review of pitch-raising surgery in male-to-female transsexual patients found mixed results, while a 2025 meta-analysis reported that surgery generally produced larger and more lasting pitch gains than voice therapy.[1][2]

paras: Other pitch-raising operations include Wendler glottoplasty (the most common today), laser reduction glottoplasty, feminization laryngoplasty, laser tuning and resonance surgery.[1] Surgery is often considered after voice therapy.[1]

A systematic review (Journal of Voice, 2017) assessed the effectiveness of pitch-raising surgery in male-to-female transsexual patients.[2] Wikipedia summarises a 2025 meta-analysis (Lanham et al.) finding that both therapy and surgery raise pitch and quality of life, with objective pitch change correlating with patient-reported outcomes, while longitudinal data remain limited.[1] A broader review covers surgical options for transgender patients.[3]
Reported risks across voice feminisation surgery include reduced voice quality and loudness, swallowing or breathing problems, sore throat, infection and scarring.[1]

timeline.event: CTA outcomes study (Van Borsel et al.).[1]
Systematic review of pitch-raising surgery published.[2]
Meta-analysis of therapy versus surgery (Lanham et al.).[1]

card.summary: Surgery that tightens the vocal folds to raise pitch; largely superseded and can leave a falsetto voice.
card.note: Irreversible surgery; outcomes may decline over time.

quick.overview:
CTA moves two laryngeal cartilages together to tension the vocal folds and raise pitch, mainly for voice feminisation.

Reviews report mixed results for older techniques, and fewer surgeons offer it now.
quick.mechanism: Bringing the cricoid and thyroid cartilages closer lengthens and tenses the folds, raising pitch.
quick.risks: Reported risks include falsetto-locked voice, loss of loudness or quality, swallowing or breathing problems, infection and scarring; effects may decline over time.
